title: Open Rank Position in Health Economics
description:
The Department of Economics at Rice University in Houston, Texas,
invites applications for a tenured or tenure-track faculty position
in Health Economics, beginning July 1, 2027. The rank is open.
Candidates at the Assistant Professor level should have completed
the Ph.D. in Economics or a closely related field by the date of
appointment. Candidates at the Associate or Full Professor level
should have a record of scholarship commensurate with appointment
at that rank at a leading research department.

We seek a scholar whose research addresses substantive questions in
health economics, broadly defined, including but not limited to the
industrial organization of health care markets, health insurance
design, the determinants and consequences of health over the life
cycle, and the evaluation of health policy. The successful
candidate will join an established group in health economics and
will have opportunities for collaboration across the University,
including with the Baker Institute for Public Policy and with
Population Health, and with institutions in the Texas Medical
Center.

Responsibilities include research, teaching at the undergraduate
and graduate levels, and service to the Department and the
University. Applicants should submit a cover letter, curriculum
vitae, job market paper or representative publications, and a
teaching statement. Applications received by November 15, 2026 will
receive full consideration.

Also, in our candidate pools, we seek to attract greater
representation of women, scholars of color, people with
disabilities, veterans, and others who have historically been
underrepresented in Economics. Rice is located in Houston, one of
the most diverse metropolitan areas in the United States.

Rice University is an Equal Opportunity Employer with
commitment to diversity at all levels, and considers for employment
qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, age,
sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national or ethnic
origin, genetic information, disability or protected veteran
status.
